limitations_and_boundaries: The paper does not combine GCNII with attention mechanisms.
The behavior of GCNII with ReLU operation is not analyzed.
The theoretical analysis of over-smoothing is limited to GCN with residual connection, not the full GCNII model.
The paper does not explore the effect of different αℓ and βℓ schedules beyond the proposed log setting.
The full-supervised experiments use a fixed random split; results may vary with different splits.
The inductive learning experiment uses only 9 layers; deeper models are not tested.
The paper does not provide runtime or memory cost analysis.

methods.name: GCNII
methods.protocol_description: GCNII extends vanilla GCN with two modifications: (1) initial residual connection that combines the smoothed representation with the first layer H(0) using a hyperparameter αℓ; (2) identity mapping that adds an identity matrix to the weight matrix W(ℓ) with a hyperparameter βℓ. The ℓ-th layer is defined as H(ℓ+1) = σ(((1-αℓ)˜P H(ℓ) + αℓ H(0)) ((1-βℓ)In + βℓ W(ℓ))). βℓ is set as log(λ/(ℓ+1)) ≈ λ/ℓ.

methods.name: GCNII*
methods.protocol_description: Variant of GCNII that employs different weight matrices for the smoothed representation and the initial residual. The (ℓ+1)-th layer is H(ℓ+1) = σ((1-αℓ)˜P H(ℓ) ((1-βℓ)In + βℓ W1(ℓ)) + αℓ H(0) ((1-βℓ)In + βℓ W2(ℓ))).

provenance.text_excerpt: 1) Directly applying identity mapping to the vanilla GCN retards the effect of over-smoothing marginally. 2) Directly applying initial residual connection to the vanilla GCN relieves over-smoothing significantly. However, the best performance is still achieved by the 2-layer model. 3) Applying identity mapping and initial residual connection simultaneously ensures that the accuracy increases with the network depths.
